bottleneck: Chronic neuroinflammation — activated microglia, complement, cytokines — accompanies every neurodegenerative disease, but whether it drives damage, responds to it, or both is unresolved. Anti-inflammatory trials have largely failed, possibly because inflammation is protective early and destructive late, or because the relevant pathways differ by disease and stage. The immune-brain axis is too poorly mapped to drug rationally, and blanket immunosuppression risks removing protective functions.
current_state: TREM2 and other microglial targets are in trials, but no anti-neuroinflammatory therapy is approved. The field lacks biomarkers distinguishing helpful from harmful inflammation in living patients.

title: Neuroinflammation's causal role unresolved
why_it_blocks: If inflammation drives neurodegeneration, taming it could treat many diseases at once. Without causal clarity, the immune-brain axis remains a graveyard of failed trials, and each failure teaches too little.
